correctness.rationale: Exact geodesic chords and the Staudtian formula yield equation (1). Uniform bound r*-r_R<=32/(1+min_i sinhR sin(g_i/2))^2 implies C(1+e^R g_min)^-2, integrable in each boundary chart. In a gap g_i=x e^-R, two u-parameters converge to z(x), the third to zero; this establishes delta(x). Dirichlet-simplex integration and dominated convergence yield C=3I/pi. Integration by parts evaluates I. Pointwise convergence of the normalized marked densities, with total integral one, yields total-variation convergence via Scheffe. Independently constructed hyperboloid-geodesic normal computations numerically match Staudtian inradii; profile, integral and Monte Carlo checks ran from actual local checker. The proof, not simulation, establishes infinite-dimensional R limit.

originality.rationale: The novelty here is strictly the sharp finite-radius expectation deficit with its exact constant, and the deficit-size-biased angular boundary law in total variation. Own prior item da972935... proves the fixed-configuration e^(2R) limit and heavy-tail law, but does not assert mean convergence, this e^(-R) coefficient, or the deficit-weighted mark. Because the limiting rescaled deficit has infinite first moment, these are not consequences of convergence in distribution; direct boundary-layer analysis is essential. Horvath supplies deterministic inradius trigonometry; Brody-Schettler address rational fixed-inradius families; closest indexed works on the same sampling geometry instead address acuteness, and other inradius works are Euclidean.

value.rationale: The expectation is a natural, directly measurable inradius statistic in the canonical 3-point hyperbolic-circle model. Existing almost-sure e^(2R) scaling has an infinite-mean limit and cannot describe the expectation; the exact e^(-R) coefficient identifies a mathematically important nonuniform-integrability crossover. The additional deficit-weighted total-variation law completely specifies the rare configurations responsible, including angular scale, profile and independent remaining angle. Neither a routine reparameterization nor a known-table recomputation.
